cues.text: Hemming pants is the most common tailoring job. A good pin job means the tailor gets it right the first time.
One. The customer wears the shoes they will wear with these pants. Different shoes change the length.
Two. They stand up straight, feet together, looking forward. No bending to look down.
Three. The pants sit at the waist the way they will wear them, with the belt on.
Four. Ask how they like it: just touching the shoe, a small fold, or a full fold.
This is called the break. No break just touches the shoe. A slight break has a small fold. A full break has a deep fold.
Kneel to the side of the customer, not in front.
Fold the extra fabric up and inside, to the length they want.
Pin across the fold, at the front, the sides, and the back. Point the pins sideways so they cannot poke.
Ask the customer to look in the mirror. Fix it until they are happy.
Pin the other leg too. Legs are often not the same.
Measure how much you folded up on each leg, and write it on the ticket, like: hem one and a half inches, both legs.
For jeans, ask if they want to keep the original hem, the factory look. Write it on the ticket, because the tailor uses a different method.
